subject: ent
title: External nose, nasal septum and choanal atresia

steps.tx: The outer nose drapes skin over the nasal bones with upper and lower lateral cartilages, and it suffers trauma and sun related cancers. Inside, the **septum** of quadrilateral cartilage with perpendicular plate and **vomer** divides the airstream. Deviations are near universal but count only when they obstruct airflow, cause contact headache, or block sinus surgery. **Little area** on the front septum carries the Kiesselbach plexus that bleeds so readily.
steps.say: The outer nose is skin over nasal bones and upper and lower side cartilages, and it suffers trauma and sun related cancers. Inside, the septum guides the airstream with quadrilateral cartilage above and bone below. Most people carry a slight deviation that causes no trouble at all. Deviation matters when it blocks airflow, triggers contact headache, or bars access for sinus surgery. The front septum carries a rich plexus that bleeds readily when disturbed.

steps.tx: The sagittal diagram maps the **quadrilateral cartilage** in front with the perpendicular plate above and the **vomer** below, the three parts of the septum. A dense red network marks the **Kiesselbach plexus** in Little area, the commonest anterior bleed site. In the exam, link anterior epistaxis with this plexus and posterior bleeds with deeper vessels that need packing or ligation.
steps.say: This sagittal diagram presents the septal cartilage in front with the perpendicular plate above and the vomer below. A dense red network indicates the Kiesselbach plexus in Little area near the nostril. This plexus causes most anterior nosebleeds, which stop with pressure or cautery. Posterior bleeds arise from deeper vessels and often need packing or ligation in theatre.

steps.tx: A broken nose is a bedside diagnosis from deformity, swelling, epistaxis, and possible **septal haematoma**. Doctors check within hours for haematoma and reassess after swelling settles at about a week, since closed reduction works best within roughly **two weeks** in adults. A haematoma needs urgent **drainage** because trapped blood starves cartilage of its perichondrial nutrition and causes necrosis, saddle deformity, or abscess, especially in children.
steps.say: A broken nose is diagnosed at the bedside from deformity, swelling, and bleeding, with a check for blood collecting under the septal lining. Doctors assess the nose within hours for such a collection and again after swelling settles at about a week. Closed reduction works best within roughly two weeks in adults. A septal collection requires urgent drainage because trapped blood starves cartilage and causes death of tissue, saddle deformity, or abscess. Children carry the highest risk of lasting deformity.

steps.tx: Holes in the septum follow surgery, trauma, picking, cocaine, or granulomatous disease, and they announce themselves with crusting, whistling, and **epistaxis**. Small symptomatic holes respond to humidification and **obturators**, while surgery closes selected larger defects. Cocaine use must stop and **vasculitis** needs control before any repair, or the closure fails and the hole returns.
steps.say: Holes in the septum follow surgery, trauma, picking, cocaine use, or granulomatous disease. They announce themselves with crusting, whistling, and repeated nosebleeds. Small troublesome holes improve with humidification and plug devices that cover the defect. Larger holes need surgical closure in selected patients. Cocaine use must stop and vasculitis needs full control before any repair, or the closure fails and the hole returns.

steps.tx: **Choanal atresia** seals the back of the nose with a bony or membranous plate. Bilateral disease distresses the newborn, an obligate nose breather, with cyclical cyanosis that crying relieves and a tube that will not pass. Unilateral disease declares itself later with one sided discharge. The **CHARGE association** links it with eye, heart, growth, and ear anomalies, and surgeons open the airway by endoscopic perforation with **stenting**.
steps.say: Choanal atresia blocks the back of the nose with a plate of bone or membrane. Bilateral disease distresses the newborn, who breathes only through the nose and turns blue when quiet but pink when crying. A feeding tube fails to pass through the blocked side. Unilateral disease appears later with a one sided discharge. The CHARGE association links it with eye, heart, growth, and ear anomalies. Surgeons open the airway with endoscopic perforation and keep it open with a stent.

vis.alt: Diagram of choanal atresia showing a bony or membranous plate obstructing the posterior nasal airway, preventing airflow from nasal cavity to nasopharynx.
vis.caption: Choanal atresia: posterior nasal airway blockage

steps.tx: Modern **septoplasty** straightens an obstructing septum while preserving an L shaped strut of cartilage that prevents saddle collapse. Older submucosal resection is largely historical because it deformed support. **Rhinoplasty** reshapes the outer framework for breathing and appearance together. Packs, splints, and saline rinses support healing, and surgeons counsel about **perforation** and residual deviation before operating.
steps.say: Modern septoplasty straightens an obstructing septum while preserving an L shaped strut that prevents saddle collapse. Older resection techniques are largely historical because they deformed support and invited collapse. Rhinoplasty serves both breathing and appearance by reshaping the outer framework. Packs, splints, and saline rinses support healing after surgery. Surgeons explain the risks of perforation and residual deviation before operating.
